messages.author: b063227c9709ab9e
messages.subject: Spatial autocorrelation
parts:
Hi there,

I have conducted multi-season, single-species occupancy (dynamic occupancy) models to estimate the probability of occurrence for various species on a small, enclosed game reserve in South Africa from camera trap data. The cameras were placed on average less than 3km apart, which means that the assumption of independence between sampling sites is violated, which could mean biased estimates of covariate associations?

Are there any analytical approaches that could be used to account for spatial autocorrelation?

Any help or advice will be greatly appreciated.

Kind regards,
Jess

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Spatial autocorrelation
parts:
Hi Jess,

 the non-independence will not lead to biased covariate effects, but may produce slightly biased estimates of SEs (they will be too small).  3 km seems like a good spacing for a lot of species -- what are you studying? Are you catching the same individuals on multiple camera traps?

 To account for this you might have to go outside of unmarked and think about fitting an occupancy model with spatial dependence built-in.  We do show how to do this in JAGS in Chapter 10 of AHM Volume 2 which is in production now but not yet published. I think we can give you some material for that let me get back to you...

There is a good paper by Johnson et al. who write their own MCMC and produce an R package for fitting models with dependence:

Johnson, D.S., Conn, P.B., Hooten, M.B., Ray, J.C. & Pond, B.A. 2013. Spatial occupancy models for large data sets. Ecology, 94, 801–808.

 and I'm sure there are other things too....

 If you stick with unmarked then you can't really deal with autocorrelation formally... maybe someone else will have some ideas?


regards

andy

messages.author: b063227c9709ab9e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Spatial autocorrelation
parts:
Hi Andy,

I studied medium to large sized carnivores, and yes we captured the same individuals on multiple camera traps. I based my dynamic occupancy analyses for my PhD thesis on the paper Schuette et al. 2013 who's cameras were placed in 4km2 grids and ours were placed in 9km2 grids. Schuette et al. 2013 also studied medium and large sized carnivores. A reviewer of my PhD thesis was worried that the lack of independence might lead to biased estimates of covariate associations and so that's why I posted my query as I am wanting to write up my chapter for publication and want to make sure that the analyses I did are correct.

Kind regards,
Jess

Hi Jess,

This topic comes up every now and then in this group, so I suggest you search the group for "spatial autocorrelation" to find the relevant threads and the functional (but perhaps inelegant) ways to address it in using unmarked. Just to be clear, the potential concern (violating assumptions) is in non-independence of model *residuals*.

Here's one of them:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/unmarked/spatial$20autocorrelation%7Csort:date/unmarked/KYrrgnxVzAg/LwCw5Rt0AAAJ

Giancarlo
